newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims skewed by November holidays.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims skewed by November holidays.

text.p: A drop of 8,000 in initial claims for unemployment insurance in the week ended November 30 was primarily due to a holiday-stunted workweek and did not mark any significant trend, economists said.
"It's difficult to read too much into these number because we had the Veterans Day holiday in the week ended November 16 and then the Thanksgiving holiday," said Alan Ruskin, an economist at I.D.E.A.
Ruskin noted increases reported by some states were attributed to workers returning to a five-day workweek after a shorter reporting period after Veterans Day.

The U.S. Labor Department said jobless claims fell to 336,000 in the week ended November 30 from an upwardly revised 344,000 in the prior week. The four-week moving average rose to 337,750 from a revised 336,750.
Economists said the four-week average reflected a static but still tight labor market.
"Claims have been pretty stable and I think the pattern remains that because the four-week average hasn't budged much," said Michael Niemira, economist at Bank of Tokyo/Mitsubishi Ltd.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond dipped nearly 1/4 point after the data were released. However, bond market analysts blamed the weakness on profit-taking and lack of a Federal Reserve coupon pass.
